authoredPrompt: This figure is a dimensioned elevation drawing of a natural draft cooling tower, rendered as a translucent orange solid of revolution. The silhouette is widest at ground level, sweeps inward to a narrow waist above the midpoint, then flares slightly outward again to a flat circular top. The left half of the shell carries many closely spaced vertical contour lines following the curvature, while the right half is left as a smooth tinted surface, and a row of small teal angled supports rings the open base. A vertical dashed line runs up the center as the axis, and a horizontal dashed line crosses it at the waist. Four measurements are marked with double-headed arrows: 72 m across the top rim, 60 m across the narrow waist, 79.6 m from the top down to the waist level, and 179.6 m for the full height from ground to top, drawn along a long dimension line at the far left. Placing both diameters and both heights against the same profile makes the whole shape recoverable from four numbers. The layout supplies the data for fitting a hyperbola, centered where the dashed lines intersect, to the curved sides of the tower.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for height along the tower axis: the learner drags a horizontal measurement line from base to top and the current diameter updates against the curved side, making clear how the radius changes with vertical position on the hyperbolic profile.
- Toggle between full tower and fitted hyperbola profile: the learner switches from the translucent solid of revolution to the 2D side curve with the 60 m waist, 72 m top, and height marks, making clear how the four dimensions determine the model.
authoredContext:
The design layout of a cooling tower is shown in the figure. The tower stands 179.6 meters tall. The diameter of the top is 72 meters. At their closest, the sides of the tower are 60 meters apart.

Project design for a natural draft cooling tower

A diagram illustrating the dimensions of a hyperbolic cooling tower, showing a total height of 179.6 m, an upper section height of 79.6 m, an upper diameter of 72 m, and a narrower waist diameter of 60 m.

Find the equation of the hyperbola that models the sides of the cooling tower. Assume that the center of the hyperbola—indicated by the intersection of dashed perpendicular lines in the figure—is the origin of the coordinate plane. Round final values to four decimal places.

discrepancies: Source meridian lines are perfectly straight vertical lines on the left half; generated lines follow the curved hyperbola profile, changing the visual character of the left side
Source base support legs are taller, more numerous-looking chevron-like braces; generated supports are short thin tilted cylinders

evaluation.notes: A faithful front-on dimensioned hyperbolic cooling tower with correct dims, colors, and a pedagogically useful height/diameter slider plus profile toggle; only minor stylization differences in meridian lines and base supports.

Reduce visual conflict between the fixed 60 m waist dimension and the movable blue measurement line (e.g., hide the slider line when at the waist height)
